rationale: The book entry's core claim — that lamp oil is not the Holy Spirit Himself but the Spirit's produced fruit: truth and correction worked into stored, proven obedience — explains the supplied texts better than the dominant Spirit-identification. The mechanics of Matthew 25 (oil must be bought, gathered beforehand, kept in one's own vessel, cannot be lent, and runs short when divided) contradict the Spirit reading on the parable's own terms: the Spirit is an unpurchasable gift (Acts 8:20), given without measure (John 3:34), and receivable in a moment (Acts 10:44), whereas the entry's referent — a life of obedience stored over time — matches every mechanic. The cited law texts independently separate lamp oil from anointing oil (Ex 25:6; 27:20 vs Ex 30:22-33), removing the anointing-Spirit chain that carries the popular reading. Prov 6:23 + Ps 141:5 supply a printed lamp/light/oil triad in which reproof is expressly called oil; Prov 21:20 stages wise/foolish/stored-oil before the parable; Prov 23:23, Ps 119:11, Prov 7:1-3, Jer 31:33 support inward storing of truth; Ezek 36:27 keeps the Spirit as cause and the walking/doing as His fruit; Zech 4's angel identifies the branches as 'the two anointed ones,' never equating oil with the Spirit; Matt 5:16 supports burning as visible example. Every material assertion actually printed in the entry is carried by the printed references, so the scope is FULL.
book_core_identification: Lamp oil symbolizes the Spirit's fruit rather than the Spirit Himself: Spirit-taught truth and received correction worked into tested, proven obedience, stored inwardly in one's own vessel over a life of hearing and doing.
book_secondary_elaborations: The oil is 'tested, pressed' — obedience proven under pressure, matching the 'pure oil olive beaten for the light' of Ex 27:20 and the reproof-as-oil of Ps 141:5
The oil is 'stored as evidence of faithful obedience' — laid up beforehand in the heart/vessel (Ps 119:11; Prov 7:1-3; 21:20; Jer 31:33)
The oil is 'burned to give a visible example that lights the Way' — obedience made visible as light before others (Matt 5:16; Prov 6:23, whose full verse ends 'the way of life')
chapter_only_objections: Reliance on Shem Tov's Hebrew Matthew ('bridegroom and the bride'; 'lazy fools'; the verb nid'akhu) as textual evidence — a disputed late medieval witness not established by the supplied excerpts
The identification of the ten virgins with the ten tribes / 'virgin of Israel' via 1 Kings 11:31 and Jeremiah 31 is a typological extension beyond the glossary entry
The Gethsemane-as-oil-press typology (the Lord crushed on the Mount of Olives yielding the 'oil' of perfect obedience) is homiletically suggestive but not demonstrated from the printed references
The claim that the wise virgin is portrayed in Proverbs 31:18 is an application deferred to another chapter
The ranking table of common interpretations is the author's characterization, not scriptural evidence
strongest_counter_interpretation: Lamp oil symbolizes the Holy Spirit Himself — His indwelling presence and sustaining grace — grounded in Zechariah 4's oil-fed lampstand read with 'not by might... but by my spirit,' the anointing-Spirit link of 1 Sam 16:13 and Acts 10:38, and the tabernacle lamp's perpetual oil (Ex 27:20); on this reading the wise virgins possess the Spirit and the foolish are professors without His indwelling.
counter_core_identification: The oil in the virgins' lamps is the Holy Spirit Himself (His presence and grace), not a product of His work.
material_core_denial: The counter asserts the oil IS the Spirit; the book asserts the oil is expressly NOT the Spirit but His fruit — obedience formed and stored. Both cannot be true of the same referent, since the book's case rests on properties (purchasable, storable, finite, non-transferable, accumulated over time) that it argues the Spirit categorically lacks.
counter_case: Zech 4 places oil, lampstand, and the word 'by my spirit' in one vision, the most natural prima facie oil-Spirit link
Anointing oil is repeatedly joined to the Spirit's coming (1 Sam 16:13; Acts 10:38; Isa 61:1), building a broad oil-Spirit association
The tabernacle's perpetual lamp (Ex 27:20) is traditionally read as continual Spirit-sustained life
The Spirit reading gives the parable a clean soteriological point: the foolish lack the indwelling Spirit and so are unknown by the Bridegroom
It is the dominant popular interpretation, recognized as primary by all four common-interpretation responses
book_explanatory_advantages: Explains why the oil must be bought (Matt 25:9; Prov 23:23 'buy the truth') when the Spirit explicitly cannot be purchased (Acts 8:20)
Explains why the oil is finite and non-transferable — one person's stored obedience cannot burn for another — whereas the Spirit is given 'not by measure' and falls in a moment (Acts 10:44)
Honors the law's own distinction between oil for the light and anointing oil as separate provisions (Ex 25:6; 30:22-33), which the Spirit reading must collapse
Accounts for the printed lamp/light/oil triad: commandment = lamp, law lived = light (Prov 6:23), reproof = excellent oil (Ps 141:5)
Explains Prov 21:20's pre-staging of the exact inventory: oil stored in the dwelling of the wise, spent up by the fool
Fits the fool/wise definition running through the cited texts as hearing-without-doing vs doing (1 John 2:4; John 12:50), so the missing oil is missing obedience, not a missing gift
Handles Zech 4 precisely: the angel identifies the branches as 'the two anointed ones,' never stating 'the oil is the Spirit,' and keeps the Spirit as the power behind appointed servants
Preserves the Spirit as cause without making Him the substance: Ezek 36:27 has the Spirit within causing the walking and doing — the oil is the caused walk
counter_explanatory_advantages: Simpler and more familiar; aligns with the broadest devotional association of oil and Spirit
Requires no distinction between oil types, treating all sacred oil imagery as one symbol
Zech 4:6 read loosely gives a direct-seeming proof text
decisive_sources: Exodus 25:6 with Exodus 30:22-33 (lamp oil and anointing oil as separate provisions, severing the anointing-Spirit chain from lamp oil)
Matthew 25:8-9 with Acts 8:20 and John 3:34 (buyable, finite, non-lendable oil vs the unpurchasable, unmeasured Spirit)
Proverbs 6:23 with Psalm 141:5 (commandment=lamp, law=light, reproof=oil — a printed triad locating oil as received correction)
Proverbs 21:20 (oil stored by the wise, spent by the fool — the parable's inventory pre-staged)
Proverbs 23:23 with Psalm 119:142 context (buying truth = acquiring the law kept)
Ezekiel 36:27 and Jeremiah 31:33 (Spirit as cause, inwardly stored law and obedience as the product)
Zechariah 4:11-14 (the angel's actual identification — 'the two anointed ones' — never 'the oil is the Spirit')
1 John 2:4 and Matthew 5:16 (profession without indwelt truth vs obedience shining as visible light)
unresolved_objections: Zechariah 4:6's juxtaposition of oil imagery with 'by my spirit' remains rhetorically suggestive for the counter even if the angel never equates oil with the Spirit
The exact phrase 'fruit of the Spirit' (Gal 5:22) is not among the printed references, though Ezek 36:27 carries the same cause-and-product structure

The book's reading requires the parable's 'buy' to be pressed literally against the Spirit reading while treating the sellers themselves non-literally; a defender of the Spirit reading could claim symmetrical selectivity, though the book's account of the purchase price (Isa 55:1-3, a life of hearing) partially answers this
